newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar seen steady to firmer versus yen in Asia.
newsitem.headline: Dollar seen steady to firmer versus yen in Asia.

text.p: The dollar is expected to be steady to firmer against the yen during Asian trading time on Tuesday, with the market seeking fresh factors to trade on, dealers said.

The dollar's downside is likely to hold firm after a close above 116 yen in New York on Monday. Bids from Japanese investors and trust banks are expected to emerge on the downside to support the greenback, they added.
"If the dollar breaks above 116.50 yen, it will head towards 117 yen," a city bank dealer said.
He added, however, that profit-taking and exporter sales were likely to limit the dollar's advance.
A trust bank dealer said: "It may be too early to say that 115 yen is becoming a floor for the dollar, but it is firming up."
Dealers said the market, however, needs fresh trading incentives to aggressively test the dollar's upside.
"Some traders may be slow to act after the national holiday (on Monday), and without fresh factors, it may be hard to get a decisive move," the trust bank dealer said.

In New York on Monday, the greenback ended an extremely thin U.S. session marginally higher, reaping modest gains from a French audit of public finances, but sticking to recent ranges ahead of Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's semi-annual Humphrey-Hawkins testimony.

The French audit revealed on Monday that the country's budget deficit was running at 3.5 to 3.7 percent of gross domestic product for 1997, well above the 3.0 percent target mandated for entry into the single European currency. This fuelled expectations that Europe's currency plan would start on schedule, but with a weak, broad-based euro.
Greenspan is scheduled to appear before a House of Representatives banking subcommittee at 1800 GMT to testify on monetary policy and economic conditions.
The city bank dealer said his testimony's direct impact on currencies may be limited, but if U.S. stocks fall in reaction to his comments, that may trigger profit-taking sales of the dollar.
